$schema: Docwriter directive-injection task graph — adds mid-run directive injection to the 29-agent pipeline
description: Adds a mid-run directive injection mechanism. Users edit .docwriter/directives.md while the pipeline is running; the orchestrator and all coordinators read it on every invocation, integrating new instructions into the existing plan. Enables scope changes, process overrides, context injection, and task-specific guidance without restarting the pipeline.
assumptions: 29 docwriter agents already exist (post task-graph-manual.json implementation)
VS Code Copilot Chat is the invocation surface
User has filesystem access to .docwriter/ between agent invocations
Each agent invocation is a separate Copilot Chat turn — user can edit files between turns
Directives are human-authored free text, not machine-generated

designDecisions.decision: Single file (.docwriter/directives.md) rather than drop folder
designDecisions.rationale: One file is easier to find, edit, and reason about. No consumption tracking needed — directives are live as long as they're in the file. User manages lifecycle by editing/deleting content.

designDecisions.decision: Section-based scoping (## Global, ## Pass N, ## Task T-NNN, ## Context)
designDecisions.rationale: Natural markdown structure the user already knows. Global applies everywhere, pass-scoped applies to that pass's coordinator, task-scoped is inlined by execution-coordinator, context enriches all agents' understanding.

designDecisions.decision: Orchestrator + 6 coordinators + knowledge-curator read the file directly (8 agents)
designDecisions.rationale: These are the routing decision-makers. Specialists receive applicable directives relayed by their coordinator in the dispatch message — no specialist file changes needed.

designDecisions.decision: Directives cannot override invariants (invariant supremacy preserved)
designDecisions.rationale: Invariants are extracted from canonical policy documents. Human directives are ad-hoc. If they conflict, the invariant wins and a warning is logged. This prevents accidental quality degradation.

Consumed-once requires tracking state and risks directives being lost if a pass re-runs. Persistent-until-removed is simpler and more predictable — user deletes a directive when it's no longer needed.

designDecisions.decision: Bootstrap creates directives.md with format template; --clean preserves it
designDecisions.rationale: Directives may contain session-spanning intent that survives pipeline re-runs, similar to meta/ preservation.

designDecisions.decision: Invariant guard + directivesApplied tracking baked into each agent task, not retrofitted
designDecisions.rationale: Eliminates a separate cross-cutting sweep phase. Each agent task includes invariant supremacy enforcement and status schema extension as part of its acceptance criteria.

sections.heading: ## Global
examples: Focus documentation on the REST API module only
All code examples must use TypeScript, not JavaScript

sections.heading: ## Context
sections.scope: Enriches all agents' understanding (informational, not behavioral)
examples: The authentication system was recently migrated from API keys to OAuth 2.0

sections.heading: ## Pass N (or ## Pass N.N)
examples: ## Pass 4\n- Skip persona review for all tasks
## Pass 6\n- Force convergence after this cycle

sections.heading: ## Task T-NNN
examples: ## Task T-003\n- Include a complete OAuth 2.0 code example
## Task T-007\n- This page targets admins, not developers

sections.heading: ## Routing
examples: Skip Pass 0 (meta-knowledge not useful for this run)
Re-run Pass 2 with broader analysis scope
Halt before Pass 7 — I want to review first

rules: Directives CANNOT override invariants — invariant supremacy is absolute
Conflicting directives are logged as warnings; the more specific scope wins (Task > Pass > Global)
Empty file or missing file = no directives (pipeline runs normally)
Agents treat directive content as authoritative human instructions

tasks.title: Add directive reading, routing overrides, conflict detection + invariant enforcement to orchestrator
tasks.description: Add a 'Read Directives' step to the orchestrator's startup sequence (after validate context, before routing table scan). Parse directives.md by section. Handle ## Routing directives: skip-pass, halt-before-pass, force-rerun. Detect conflicting directives (e.g., 'skip Pass 2' + 'force-rerun Pass 2') and log warnings. Any directive conflicting with an invariant is flagged and ignored. Log active directives in manifest.json. Add directivesApplied tracking to progress.json.
acceptanceCriteria: Startup sequence includes 'Read Directives' step after context validation
## Routing directives handled: skip-pass (sets pass to done), halt-before-pass (stops routing), force-rerun (resets pass status)
Active directives logged in manifest.json on each invocation
Missing or empty directives.md is a no-op (pipeline runs normally)
Conflicting routing directives detected and logged as warnings
More specific scope wins on conflict (explicit pass directive beats global)
Invariant-conflicting directives flagged and ignored with manifest entry
Invalid directives (nonexistent pass, malformed section) logged as warnings, not errors
progress.json gains directives section tracking active directive count and last-read timestamp
Status includes directivesApplied array: { section, summary, action } for each applied directive
